title: When Is Noise Response Universal? Tokenization as the Hidden Variable in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.26319v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The performance of textual neural models often degrades when their inputs are corrupted by noise such as typos, OCR errors, or dropped words. We study the degradation rate across neural models, both sentence embeddings and decoder-only LLMs, and find that how consistent it is depends on the scale of the noise: under word-level noise, models with very different architectures decline along nearly the same curve, while under character-level noise they separate. We further identify the determining factor to be the training objective, not the architecture: eight encoders spanning six pretraining paradigms are scattered initially, and collapse onto a common curve after a short contrastive training recipe. We trace the word/character split to tokenization: a single character edit forces the tokenizer to re-segment the surrounding word, disturbing the token sequence far more than dropping a whole word does. translated_title: 噪声响应何时具有普遍性？分词作为语言模型中的隐藏变量
translated_abstract: 文本神经模型的性能常常在输入受到噪声（如拼写错误、OCR错误或单词缺失）干扰时下降。我们研究了多种神经模型（包括句子嵌入和仅解码器的大型语言模型）的性能退化率，发现其一致性取决于噪声的尺度：在词级噪声下，架构差异很大的模型沿几乎相同的曲线下降；而在字符级噪声下，它们则出现分化。我们进一步确定决定因素是训练目标而非架构：跨越六种预训练范式的八个编码器最初分散，但在简短的对比训练方案后收敛到共同曲线。我们将词级与字符级的分裂追溯到分词机制：单个字符编辑迫使分词器重新分割周围单词，对令牌序列的扰动远大于删除整个单词。这一发现及其潜在机制...
tldr: 本文发现语言模型在词级噪声下表现普遍一致，但在字符级噪声下分化，并揭示分词机制是这一差异的隐藏决定因素，而非模型架构。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that language models exhibit universal degradation under word-level noise but diverge under character-level noise, revealing tokenization as the hidden determinant rather than model architecture.
